grades.quote: Signed and unsigned integer minimum and maximum instructions are supported.
grades.reason: Lists signed and unsigned vector min/max variants, providing comparison-related operations rather than general comparison semantics.

grades.quote:
The integer minimum/maximum instructions are arithmetic R-type instructions that return the smaller/larger of two operands.

|RV32|RV64|Mnemonic|Instruction|
|---|---|---|---|
|✓|✓|max rd, rs1, rs2|Maximum|
|✓|✓|maxu rd, rs1, rs2|Unsigned maximum|
|✓|✓|min rd, rs1, rs2|Minimum|
|✓|✓|minu rd, rs1, rs2|Unsigned minimum|
grades.reason: Explains comparison-based min/max operations and identifies signed versus unsigned variants, but does not cover general comparison instructions.
Describes signed and unsigned widening multiply-add operations, not integer comparisons.

grades.quote:
Overflow checking for unsigned addition requires only a single additional branch instruction after the addition:_ `add t0, t1, t2; bltu t0, t1, overflow` _._

_For signed addition, if one operand’s sign is known, overflow checking requires only a single branch after the addition:_ `addi t0, t1, +imm; blt t0, t1, overflow` _. This covers the common case of addition with an immediate operand._
grades.reason: Shows unsigned BLTU versus signed BLT comparison usage, but focuses on overflow checking rather than explaining their comparison semantics.
